teacherNotes.content: Present the pronunciation/reading rule for: The OUGH & GH Complex Patterns. Use the 14 Gabarit fields to clarify rule, system, logic, and exceptions.

teacherNotes.title: Anticipated Problems & Solutions (CELTA Standard)
teacherNotes.content:
⚠️ Problem: Learner pronounces "though" as /θrʌf/.
💡 Solution: Drill sentence: Though (/oʊ/) it was rough (/ʌf/), he went through (/uː/).

elements.content: Gabarit 14 Champs: The OUGH & GH Complex Patterns
1. Definition: OUGH and GH are historical letter combinations with multiple distinct pronunciations.

2. Rule: GH = silent in igh/eigh/augh/ough (light, night, eight, daughter, bought); GH = /f/ in rough, tough, laugh, cough. OUGH has 6 main sounds: 1. /ʌf/ (rough), 2. /ɔː/ (bought), 3. /oʊ/ (though), 4. /uː/ (through), 5. /aʊ/ (bough), 6. /ɒf/ (cough).
3. Why? Middle English velar fricative /x/ was lost or shifted to /f/ while medieval spelling was retained.
4. How to recognize? Spot letter groups igh, eigh, augh, ough, gh.
5. Common examples: light /laɪt/, eight /eɪt/, daughter /ˈdɔːtər/, rough /rʌf/, bought /bɔːt/, though /ðoʊ/, through /θruː/, cough /kɒf/
6. Counter-examples: GH at word start where G is hard (ghost /ɡoʊst/).
7. Exceptions: hiccough (archaic spelling for hiccup /ˈhɪkʌp/).
8. Common mistakes: Trying to apply a single rule to all OUGH words.
9. Mnemonic / Hint: OUGH has 6 sounds! Memorize "though, through, rough, cough, thought, bough"!
10. Key vocabulary: OUGH pattern, silent GH, velar fricative, Middle English, irregular spelling
11. Frequency: ★★★★☆ (High)
12. CEFR Level: 🟠 B1
13. Associated Visual: 🚦 6-color branch chart showing the 6 pronunciations of OUGH.
14. Key Takeaway: OUGH is irregular! Memorize the top 10 words: though, through, rough, thought...

teacherNotes.title: Teacher CCQ Script
teacherNotes.content: Ask these concept checking questions to verify rule understanding without translation:

elements.content: Rule Understanding Check (CCQ):
CCQ 1: Does "ough" sound the same in "though" and "through"? (No, though = /oʊ/, through = /uː/)
CCQ 2: How is GH pronounced in "rough" and "cough"? (/f/ sound)
CCQ 3: How is GH pronounced in "light" and "bought"? (Silent)

teacherNotes.title: Stage aim
teacherNotes.content: Auditory discrimination, minimal pairs, and guided oral drill repetition.

elements.content: Match OUGH words with their correct sound:
🎯 Item: though ➔ Answer / Pronunciation: /oʊ/ (like go)
🎯 Item: through ➔ Answer / Pronunciation: /uː/ (like too)
🎯 Item: rough ➔ Answer / Pronunciation: /ʌf/ (like stuff)
